icosahedral.text: I consists of the 60 proper icosahedral rotations. Each rotation acts on both the seed center c and its axis u.

tetrahedral.text: T consists of the 12 proper tetrahedral rotations. The seed center c and unit axis u generate the vortex family.
tetrahedral.parameters: **Left · Case 421** σ ≈ 0.304249, γ ≈ 0.0169314. **Right · Case 565** σ ≈ 0.406287, γ ≈ 0.0423407. [Exact seeds and initial states](results/unexpected-search/facts.json)

gaussian-vortex.tex: r_j=x-d e_j,\qquad\dot x=-\gamma x+b+\sum_{j=0}^2\omega_j(e_{j+1}\times r_j)\exp\!\left(-\frac{\lVert r_j\rVert^2}{2\sigma_j^2}\right).
gaussian-vortex.text: The basis index is taken modulo three. Case 77 uses three equally strong vortices of equal width and a constant drift b with equal components.
gaussian-vortex.parameters: **Case 77** γ ≈ 0.185575, ω₀=ω₁=ω₂ ≈ 5.61179, σ₀=σ₁=σ₂ ≈ 0.690724, d ≈ 1.61178, and each drift component ≈ 0.100028. Start (0.1, 0.2, 0.3). [Exact coefficients](results/gaussian-vortex/candidates.json)

twist.text: The rotations act in the xy, yz and zx planes in that order. Each wⱼ is the remaining coordinate immediately before its rotation, r is the contraction ratio and e₁=(1,0,0).

raar.system: Relaxed averaged alternating reflections (RAAR) between two spatial circles
raar.text: P_A and P_B are nearest-point projections onto circumferences. A is the unit xy circle. B is the circle c+r(cos t, cos θ sin t, sin θ sin t).

raar-constellations.system: Unit-circle / nearest-site relaxed averaged alternating reflections (RAAR)
raar-constellations.text: P_B selects the nearest vertex of a finite spatial set. P_A(v) normalizes the xy component and sets z to zero. Case 1504 has four sites and Case 1725 has six.
raar-constellations.parameters: **Left · Case 1504** β ≈ 0.93285, 4 tetrahedral sites. **Right · Case 1725** β ≈ 0.970661, 6 octahedral sites. Both start at (0.317, −0.211, 0.419). [Exact site coordinates and coefficients](results/raar-constellations/runs/raar-constellation-long01/report.json)

soft-constellations.system: Gaussian posterior-mean reflection map with a unit circle
soft-constellations.tex: m(x)=\frac{\sum_j b_j e^{-\lVert x-b_j\rVert^2/\tau}}{\sum_j e^{-\lVert x-b_j\rVert^2/\tau}},\quad v=2m(x_n)-x_n,\quad x_{n+1}=\beta x_n+\beta P(v)+(1-2\beta)m(x_n).
soft-constellations.text: P(v) normalizes the xy component and sets z to zero. The bⱼ are equally weighted sites, τ is temperature and β is relaxation.
soft-constellations.parameters: **Left · Case 29** β ≈ 0.985124, τ ≈ 0.265201, 4 tetrahedral sites. **Right · Case 156** β ≈ 0.970661, τ ≈ 0.0373168, 6 octahedral sites. Both start at (0.317, −0.211, 0.419). [Exact site coordinates and coefficients](results/soft-constellations/runs/soft-constellation-long01/report.json)

soft-sphere.system: Gaussian posterior-mean reflection map with a unit sphere
soft-sphere.tex: m(x)=\frac{\sum_j b_j e^{-\lVert x-b_j\rVert^2/\tau}}{\sum_j e^{-\lVert x-b_j\rVert^2/\tau}},\quad v=2m(x_n)-x_n,\quad x_{n+1}=\beta x_n+\beta\frac{v}{\lVert v\rVert}+(1-2\beta)m(x_n).
soft-sphere.text: The normalized vector projects onto the unit sphere. The bⱼ are equally weighted spatial sites, τ is temperature and β is relaxation.
soft-sphere.parameters: **Left · Case 155** β ≈ 0.957378, τ ≈ 0.0127572, 8 cubic sites. **Right · Case 251** β ≈ 0.93285, τ ≈ 0.0585393, 4 tetrahedral sites. Both start at (0.317, −0.211, 0.419). [Exact site coordinates and coefficients](results/soft-sphere/runs/soft-sphere-verification01/report.json)

canonical-sphere.system: Canonical tetrahedral and cubic posterior–sphere maps
canonical-sphere.tex: m(x)=\frac{\sum_j b_j e^{-\lVert x-b_j\rVert^2/\tau}}{\sum_j e^{-\lVert x-b_j\rVert^2/\tau}},\quad v=2m(x_n)-x_n,\quad x_{n+1}=\beta x_n+\beta\frac{v}{\lVert v\rVert}+(1-2\beta)m(x_n).
canonical-sphere.text: The canonical sites are b=c+aσ. Case 163 uses the four sign triples with σ₁σ₂σ₃=1 (tetrahedron), and Case 653 uses all eight sign triples (cube). τ is temperature and β is relaxation.
canonical-sphere.parameters: **Left · Case 163** β = 0.93, τ = 0.1, a = 0.8, c = (-0.1, -0.2, 0.2) (tetrahedral sites). **Right · Case 653** β = 0.99, τ = 0.08, a = 0.35, c = (-0.5, -0.5, -0.5) (cubic sites). Both start at (0.317, −0.211, 0.419). [Exact site coordinates and coefficients](results/canonical-sphere/runs/canonical-sphere-verification01/report.json)

product-alphabet.tex: m_i(x)=\frac{\sum_{\ell\in A_i}\ell\,e^{-(x_i-\ell)^2/\tau}}{\sum_{\ell\in A_i}e^{-(x_i-\ell)^2/\tau}},\quad v=2m(x_n)-x_n,\quad x_{n+1}=\beta x_n+\beta\frac{v}{\lVert v\rVert}+(1-2\beta)m(x_n).
product-alphabet.text: Aᵢ is the stored alphabet along coordinate i. Case 988 uses two levels per coordinate and Case 489 uses four. Independent Gaussian weights give the mean m; β controls relaxation and τ is temperature.
product-alphabet.parameters: **Left · Case 988** β ≈ 0.926809, τ ≈ 0.0209357, 2 levels per axis. **Right · Case 489** β ≈ 0.969938, τ ≈ 0.0358258, 4 levels per axis. product-irregular.tex: m_i(x)=\frac{\sum_{\ell\in A_i}\ell\,e^{-(x_i-\ell)^2/\tau}}{\sum_{\ell\in A_i}e^{-(x_i-\ell)^2/\tau}},\quad v=2m(x_n)-x_n,\quad x_{n+1}=\beta x_n+\beta\frac{v}{\lVert v\rVert}+(1-2\beta)m(x_n).
product-irregular.text: The levels in each coordinate alphabet Aᵢ have nonuniform spacing. Case 6 has four levels per coordinate and Case 7 has five. Their temperatures τ differ while β is shared.

anderson.system: Three-history regularized Anderson acceleration of a scalar tanh iteration
anderson.text: The residual is rᵢ = g(xᵢ) − xᵢ for g(x) = c + k tanh(x). The coefficient λ sets the regularization.
anderson.parameters: **Left · Case 54** k ≈ 3.66546, c ≈ 2.06188, λ ≈ 0.0332963, scalar start ≈ -1.55803. **Right · Case 449** k ≈ 2.60333, c ≈ -1.05471, λ ≈ 0.00071673, scalar start ≈ 1.47542. Each initial history is (x, g(x), g(g(x))). [Exact coefficients and cold histories](results/unexpected-search/facts.json)

rk45.system: Dormand–Prince RK45 adaptive controller on a damped harmonic oscillator
rk45.text: Dormand–Prince 5(4) on the damped oscillator y = (q,p). With absolute and relative tolerances τ, ρ, accept v if w < 1 and multiply h by min(10, 0.9 w^(−1/5)), capped at one after a rejection. Otherwise retry y with factor max(0.2, 0.9 w^(−1/5)). Zero error selects the maximum allowed growth.
rk45.parameters: The normalized absolute tolerance is τ = 1. Values are ordered as `(ζ, ρ)`. Left · Case 335 `(0.8877198030073196, 1.4674009503231292e-10)`. Right · Case 448 `(0.9463349944557995, 6.210996908104011e-06)`. [Archived settings and portrait starts](results/rk45-controller/oscillator/render/analysis.json)

rk23.system: Bogacki–Shampine RK23 adaptive controller on a damped harmonic oscillator
rk23.text: Bogacki–Shampine 3(2) on the damped oscillator y = (q,p). With absolute and relative tolerances τ, ρ, accept v if w < 1 and multiply h by min(10, 0.9 w^(−1/3)), capped at one after a rejection. Otherwise retry y with factor max(0.2, 0.9 w^(−1/3)). Zero error selects the maximum allowed growth.
rk23.parameters: The normalized absolute tolerance is τ = 1. Values are ordered as `(ζ, ρ)`. Left · Case 381 `(0.4435243054088205, 3.3379616873243337e-10)`. Right · Case 883 `(0.9588936367407441, 3.71684809666591e-12)`. [Archived settings and portrait starts](results/rk23-controller/oscillator/render/analysis.json)

yogi-tanh.text: The memory coefficients are b and c. The activation scale is k = 10α² and the normalized offset is e = ε/α.

motor-three-asymmetric.text: For row j, c and s are the cosine and sine occupancy coefficients, X is displacement and V is velocity. The axes are an orthogonal rotation of the three cosine occupancies.

synchronematic.system: Four-particle synchronematic colloid model with first- and third-harmonic coupling
synchronematic.text: The four phases θ and orientations χ interact at pair distances d. For each pair, Δ is the phase difference θⱼ−θᵢ and ψ measures orientation relative to the pair direction. The source specifies both first- and third-harmonic kernels; f̄ is the four-particle mean.

After 2,000 transient and 8,000 observed cycles, the plotted segment starts at (u, v, φ) = [0.0, 0.0001097406461435281, 0.00022362066470260102]. The analytic event solver uses 256 subdivisions. The portrait samples each light-on and light-off arc at 65 points. Its scaled axes are u/q, v/(√k q) and φ/q, with q = I/(1+I). [Exact trace-generation code](research/analyze_lce_slider.py)

two-strain.tex:
\begin{aligned}
\dot S &= \mu(1-S)-\beta_1 I_1 S-F_2 S,\\
\dot I_1 &= (\beta_1 S-\mu-\gamma_1)I_1,\\
\dot I_2 &= F_2 S-(\mu+\gamma_2)I_2,\\
\dot I_{12} &= \sigma_{12}F_2R_1-(\mu+\gamma_{12})I_{12},\\
\dot R_1 &= \gamma_1I_1-\sigma_{12}F_2R_1-\mu R_1
\\ F_2&=\beta_2(I_2+\eta_2 I_{12}).
\end{aligned}
two-strain.text: The five variables are population fractions. S is susceptible, I₁ and I₂ are the two primary infections, I₁₂ is the secondary infection, and R₁ is recovery from the first infection. The portrait shows physical fractions.
two-strain.parameters: Scout 203, refinement 32, uses reproduction numbers 2.5 and 1.87125, μ = 0.00025, γ₁ = 1, γ₂ = 1.1 and σ₁₂ = η₂ = 1.1. The displayed population fractions cover 15,000 additional model-time units, sampled every 0.5. [Render integration](results/two-strain/candidate-render-trace.json)

The rendered trajectory starts from the full-spectrum run’s final log-coordinate state [0.43434895669565277, -140.36802401757126, -10.686977197961914, 0.2435751164057897, 0.1166665315801187], equivalent to (S, I₁, I₂, I₁₂, R₁) = [0.43434895669565277, 2.7345240175881133e-65, 4.319272362853382e-09, 1.3908416967608803e-09, 0.1166665315801187]. DOP853 uses relative and absolute tolerances 1e−12 and 1e−14, maximum step 0.5. [Exact initial-state file, key final_log_state](results/compact-data/7bbb19fca834e73c6221bce184a5d3e257c824a60ffea826cbc25505dbfd8e54.npz)

fastica.system: One-unit empirical FastICA with the Gaussian nonlinearity
fastica.tex: u_i=x_i^\top w,\quad h=\frac1N\sum_{i=1}^N\!\left[x_i g(u_i)-g'(u_i)w\right],\quad w^+=\frac{h}{\|h\|},\quad g(u)=u e^{-u^2/2}
fastica.text: The fixed whitened observations xᵢ lie in four dimensions. Case 204 uses N = 32 normal samples and Case 351 uses N = 16 Student-t samples. Both panels follow the first FastICA weight on the unit 3-sphere.
fastica.parameters: In four dimensions, the left panel (Case 204) uses 32 whitened normal observations (seed 1190196705), and the right panel (Case 351) uses 16 whitened Student-t observations with 2.5 degrees of freedom (seed 460786286). Both use g(u) = u exp(−u²/2). [Left data and start](results/fastica/follow-01/case-204-input.json) · [Right data and start](results/fastica/follow-01/case-351-input.json)
fastica.exact: The exact whitened observation matrices are the X arrays of the two input files. The starting weight vectors before normalization are left [-0.6660440683481935, 0.40750103987154973, -1.1463745154453362, -0.6816622331272629] and right [-0.10954381680645076, -1.4785357225268183, 0.19851379294396682, -1.964859574858424]. Each portrait discards 10,000 updates and retains 1,000,000 consecutive states at stride 1. The survey master seed was 2026110101. [Data generator](results/fastica/source-original/pilot.py) · [Histogram protocol](results/fastica/histograms/render-inputs.json)

fastica-tripling.system: One-unit cubic FastICA on a deterministic 720-observation sample
fastica-tripling.tex: h(w)=\mathbb E[X(X^\top w)^3]-3\mathbb E[(X^\top w)^2]w,\qquad w^+=\frac{h(w)}{\|h(w)\|}
fastica-tripling.text: The expectation averages the 720 specified, equally weighted four-dimensional observations. The two panels use the same cubic FastICA update and the structured data at ε = 0.04 and 0.15, respectively.
fastica-tripling.parameters: The left dataset uses ε = 0.04 and the right ε = 0.15. Both start from the unit vector obtained by normalizing (0.83, 0.29, −0.13, 0.11), discard 10,000 updates and retain 500,000 consecutive unit-weight vectors. fastica-tripling.exact: Each base point (x,y) among (±1,0), (0,±1) occurs four times, and each among (±√6,0), (0,±√6) occurs once. For each of these 20 entries, take all 36 ordered pairs (ξ,η) from the list (√3,−√3,0,0,0,0), with repetition by index. Set R = x²+y², σ = √(1−6ε²) and form observations (x,y,εx(R−4)+σξ,εy(R−4)+ση). All 720 rows have equal weight. [Deterministic data construction](docs/fastica-tripling.md#data-and-update)
